name: chart
title: Chart
description: Bars, lines, areas and rings, drawn in SVG by hand, with no charting library: grouped and stacked bars, lines with dots, curves or steps, gradient areas that can stack, radial progress, concentric rings and a stacked ring. Every colour is a token a series names by tone, so a chart follows a game's Studio palette. Every chart is also a visually hidden table, and the plot is one focusable group the arrow keys walk, announcing the point in focus and showing it in a tooltip, so nothing is hover-only. It moves once on mount (bars grow, lines draw, areas rise, rings sweep) on the fill motion token, and not at all under reduced motion. Numbers are tabular. `ChartCard` is the card shadcn puts a chart in: a heading, one line, the chart, a footer. Performs nothing: the host supplies the numbers and the words. GSUI-287.
docs: `<Chart type="line" label="Your points by round" data={rows} x="round" series={[{ key: 'you', label: 'You', tone: 'player' }]} />`. `type` is `bar`, `line`, `area` or `radial`. `data` is one row per x category; for `radial` the first row holds each ring's value and `max` is what a full ring means. `stacked` stacks bars, areas, or series sharing one ring. `curve` is `linear`, `smooth` or `step`; `dots` marks every point; `format` renders a number (e.g. `n => `${n}%``); `legend` defaults on for more than one series; `height` sets the plot height, and the width fills the container, so it works from 360px. `label` is the accessible name and the table's caption, so say what the chart shows. Tones: interactive, reward, positive, player, opponent, warning, negative, muted; the default order is player, reward, positive, opponent, warning, which stay distinct in every theme. Words for the table and the announcement come from the `chart.*` strings.
